# The two microGPT programs on the compile path

The measuring stick of the compile-path work: `explorations/run-c4/src` (the flat
Run C4 model) and `explorations/apl/mg` (the APL-notation port). Every component and
api of both, pushed through `fortress compile` in dependency order, in the same
private cache as the ladder, immediately after the ladder run of this directory.

`phase` is decided by `classify.py`, the ladder's own classifier, so these rows are
the same kind of claim as a row of `ladder.tsv`. Only `fortress compile` was run;
nothing was linked or run, so `pass` here means the component compiled, not that it
produced an answer.

Per file: `fortress compile <file>` from the file's own directory, 300 s timeout.

## What the two programs are waiting on

Written by hand.

All eighteen files stop in the same phase, `disambiguate`, on one of four names:
`Array` (8 files), `Char` (5), `ImmutableArray` (3), `Vector` (2). None reaches the
checker, so nothing is yet known about whether the compiler world can type these
programs, let alone generate code for them.

Those names are the head of the ladder's own ranking (`REPORT.md`, "The name the
file stops on"): `ImmutableArray` 26 files, `Array1` 7, `Char` 6, `Array` 5. So the
measuring stick is blocked behind exactly the wall the ladder says the corpus is
blocked behind, and behind the decision `coordinator/PLAN.md` reserves — the array
representation. `Vector` is `AplMg`'s own, from the APL port's rank vocabulary.

This is the phase a ladder-regression stage would hold: eighteen components at
`disambiguate`, and any one of them reaching the checker is a move.

Not verified: only `fortress compile` was run, in dependency order, each file from
its own directory. No component was linked or run, and nothing here says what the
next error would be once these four names bind.
